findings.description: Rewording the ArmedGitDriverError refusal dropped the space after the em dash, so it now reads 'with your environment —include.path, ...' (was `your environment — ${shown}`); restore `— ${shown}`.

The comment (and ADR 0089) says `--no-includes` keeps a fifo named by an include from blocking the check, but that holds for the `config --list` call only: the check's earlier `rev-parse --git-common-dir` (L806-810) loads config with includes and can still block on such a fifo (the hang ADR 0105 already accepts). Reword to say only the listing is protected.

readRegularFile maps every open error other than ENOENT/ENOTDIR (EACCES, EMFILE, ...) to 'irregular', so an unreadable but regular small info/attributes is refused with the false reason 'not a regular file of 1 MiB or less'; refusing is right, but the reason should also cover 'unreadable'.

Only commentOnPullRequest is tested under the fake gh that runs git, so reverting `env: pinnedGitEnv()` at ghJson, rewritePullRequest or createPullRequest (the `gh pr create` that actually runs `git status`) fails no test; the 1 MiB cap and ENOTDIR-as-missing branches of readRegularFile also have no test.

pinnedGitEnv rebuilds GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n/VALUE_n by filtering '-c' out of GIT_SAFE_CONFIG's argv form and splitting on '=', a lossy round trip resting on an unwritten invariant ('-c' never appears as a value, every entry is key=value); a [key, value] pair list as the source, with argv derived from it, would remove that.
The runGit JSDoc still says 'The one way pup runs git: GIT_SAFE_CONFIG in argv and scrubbedGitEnv in env', but spawnOptions now also lays GIT_HISTORY_ENV over every child; add it to the description.

The new header comment ('Every gh runs under pinnedGitEnv: its cwd is the main checkout, whose config a session can write, and gh runs git there') restates pinnedGitEnv's JSDoc, which AGENTS.md §Comments says to delete at the call site; it also doesn't fit assertGhAvailable's `gh --version`, which has no cwd and runs no git.

docs/adr/README.md says to number a new decision by incrementing the highest NNNN on origin/main (index runs to 0130), but this decision back-fills the gap at 0089; if 89 was not reserved, renumber to 0131 and update the Amended-by lines in 0050/0101, the index and the 'decision 89' references.

The ADR's Tests paragraph walks through each test case and its mechanism, restating the test files and bound to go stale; the closing sentence (each test except the replace-ref one fails with its fix removed) is the part worth keeping.

pinnedGitEnv carries no submodule pins, so gh's `git status` in the main checkout (gh pr create) can still recurse into a session-made gitlink whose own config/info/attributes arm a filter that runs as the operator; this predates the PR (gh ran unpinned before) and ADR 0089 doesn't claim it, but it belongs in 0089's Ceilings or as an owed item (e.g. run gh with a cwd outside the repo).

runUtility runs `claude -p` during the merge (draftDecisionRecord) with pup's cwd and the unscrubbed process.env, so when pup runs from the main checkout a session-written core.fsmonitor can run on Claude Code's own git, the same exposure decision 89 closes for gh; give it pinnedGitEnv() and a cwd outside the repo.

ADR 0089's ceilings list replace refs, grafts, commit-graph and shallow but not the object store itself: a session that can write objects/ can replace a loose commit with a forged parent list (git doesn't re-hash on rev-walk), moving the merge-base as a graft would; worth recording next to `shallow`.
